market_summary: SG bank earnings week is the dominant local catalyst: OCBC beat with record banking profit and raised 2026 guidance, while DBS and UOB missed and saw target cuts, creating a split reaction even though all three stocks fell on the day amid broader risk-off. Singapore Airlines' cabin retrofit delay to H2 2027 adds to a thin but negative news flow for the carrier just ahead of its Nov 11 results. In the US, Nvidia's tightened Southeast Asia chip-tracking is a compliance measure rather than a new demand shock, and the stock bounced +2.8% after a brutal month-long drawdown (-19%), while Tesla rallied despite confirming Cybertruck wind-down, as the market looks past the product to the Cybercab pivot. Broader indices (SPY/QQQ/ES3) are all pulling back from highs amid rate/inflation uncertainty, so single-name dispersion is doing the work right now rather than broad beta.

picks.thesis: OCBC beat Q3 estimates with record banking-ops profit (+16% YoY) and raised full-year guidance on loans, income and credit costs, yet the stock is still down -4.4% over 1m and -11.6% over 3m and fell again on results day — a disconnect between improving fundamentals and price action that looks like a buying opportunity as the market digests the numbers over the coming weeks.
picks.news: OCBC Q3 2026 net profit S$2.04bn (+3% YoY), record banking-ops profit, raised 2026 guidance (2026-11-06, Yahoo Finance SG).
picks.risks: Sector-wide NIM compression or a broader SG bank sell-off could keep OCBC down regardless of its own beat; stock is -14% from 52w high and volatility is elevated (20% annualized), so near-term downside follow-through is possible before reversion.

picks.thesis: SIA just confirmed its new A350 cabin retrofit is delayed again to H2 2027 due to certification issues, compounding an already weak analyst picture (only 1 buy vs 10 hold/3 sell, consensus target basically at spot with 0.3% implied upside). The stock has still run up +5.8% over the past month and sits above both MAs, leaving it priced for good news into Nov 11 results with little analyst conviction to support further upside.
picks.news: SIA delays new First/Business Class cabin introduction to H2 2027 on A350 certification issues (2026-11-06, CNBC).
picks.risks: Q3 results (Nov 11) could beat on strong travel demand/fuel costs, and airlines have shown resilience to retrofit-timeline noise in the past; a positive earnings surprise would invalidate the short quickly given the small market-implied move (~2%).

picks.thesis: UOB missed Q3 estimates alongside DBS, but unlike DBS has materially weaker analyst support (only 3 buy vs 10 hold/3 sell) and worse technicals — down -12.5% over 3m, still -6.8% below its 200-day average versus DBS's +5.1% above. The earnings-miss narrative plus lack of a 'buying opportunity' consensus (which analysts specifically flagged for DBS) suggests UOB underperforms its SG bank peers near-term.
picks.news: DBS and UOB miss Q3 earnings estimates; brokers cut targets but see buying opportunity specifically in DBS after the slide (2026-11-06, Business Times).
picks.risks: Broad SG bank rally (e.g., if OCBC's strong quarter lifts sentiment sector-wide) could drag UOB up regardless of relative weakness; high short-term volume (rel_volume 1.98x) shows the stock is already being actively repriced, which could resolve either direction.

picks.thesis: DBS missed Q3 estimates and fell -2.1% on the day, but unlike UOB it retains strong analyst support (10 buy/6 hold/1 sell, three brokers with targets S$79.50-86.80) and multiple commentators explicitly framed the post-results slide as a buying opportunity. Longer-term trend (+18.6% 6m, +25.5% 1y) remains intact despite the recent pullback.
picks.news: Analysts cut DBS target prices for lower 2027 earnings but see buying opportunity after the share price slide (2026-11-06, Business Times).
picks.risks: This is a lower-conviction, contrarian call against a fresh earnings miss and a -9.4% 3m trend; if NIM pressure or credit-cost guidance deteriorates further at the next update, the stock could keep grinding lower before any bounce.

picks.thesis: Nvidia's new Fleet Intelligence tracking requirement for Southeast Asian cloud partners is a compliance/anti-smuggling measure, not a new demand or export restriction — arguably reduces regulatory tail risk rather than adding to it. The stock already absorbed a brutal month (-19%) and is rebounding (+2.8% today) off oversold levels (-22% from 52w high, -15% vs 50-day MA) heading into Nov 17 earnings, with analysts still overwhelmingly bullish (59 buy/2 hold/1 sell).
picks.news: Nvidia requires SE Asia cloud partners to enroll in Fleet Intelligence chip-tracking to fight smuggling of banned processors to China (2026-11-06, Bloomberg).
picks.risks: High beta (1.59) and volatility (38% annualized) mean this is a volatile trade; any fresh China-demand headline or disappointing guidance into the Nov 17 print could reverse the bounce quickly, and the extreme analyst-target implied upside (75%) likely reflects stale estimates that haven't caught up to the de-rating.

picks.thesis: Keppel has sold off hard (-9.9% 1m, -28.2% from 52w high, at its 52w low) on no specific adverse news in this dataset, while analysts remain heavily bullish (12 buy/2 hold/1 sell) with 34.5% implied upside to consensus target — the gap between price action and analyst view is unusually wide, suggesting a potential value/mean-reversion setup, though the lack of a fresh catalyst keeps conviction low.
picks.news: No company-specific news item in this cycle; call is based purely on technical oversold readings (price at 52-week low, elevated rel_volume 2.57x) against a still-bullish analyst base.
picks.risks: This is a thin-news, purely technical/valuation call — if the heavy relative volume reflects real negative information not yet reported (e.g., a review or operational issue), the stock could keep falling and analyst targets could be cut before any rebound.
